episodes.title: Chemical treatment and severed tresses.

blocks.text:
The customer requested a 4-inch trim from the bottom. Instead, the stylist chopped her hair to just 1 inch from the scalp.

episodes.title: The Supreme Court Verdict: ₹2 Cr Set Aside, Reduced to ₹25 Lakhs.

blocks.text:
A Supreme Court bench of Justices Aniruddha Bose and Vikram Nath held that while ITC was unquestionably guilty of Deficiency in Service, compensation must be based on quantifiable material evidence.

The apex court held that consumer courts cannot award arbitrary windfall damages without examining tax returns and actual financial loss. The award was reduced to ₹25 Lakhs.

blocks.text:
सुप्रीम कोर्ट के न्यायमूर्ति अनिरुद्ध बोस और विक्रम नाथ की पीठ ने फैसला सुनाया कि हालांकि आईटीसी सेवा में कमी की दोषी थी, लेकिन मुआवजा ठोस दस्तावेजी सबूतों पर आधारित होना चाहिए।

अदालत ने कहा कि उपभोक्ता आयोग बिना टैक्स रिटर्न या वित्तीय नुकसान की जांच किए मनमाना हर्जाना नहीं दे सकते। मुआवजे को घटाकर ₹25 लाख कर दिया गया।

flashcards.q: Which court decided The ₹2 Crore Haircut Case and in what year?
flashcards.a: Supreme Court of India in the year 2023.

flashcards.q: What was the primary legal issue addressed in this case?
What is the core Ratio Decidendi of the judgment?
flashcards.a: The Supreme Court confirmed Deficiency in Service but set aside the ₹2 Crore award for lack of material evidence. The matter was remanded and subsequently compensation was determined at ₹25 Lakhs.

flashcards.q: What is the primary citation for this ruling?
flashcards.a: ITC Ltd. v. Aashna Roy, 2023 INSC 124, Civil Appeal No. 6371 of 2021

flashcards.q: What is the current legal status of this precedent?
flashcards.a: Supreme Court confirmed deficiency in service but mandated quantifiable proof for major compensation.
